## Overview

Swift 6.4 is now generally available, according to a [Swift.org blog post](https://www.swift.org/blog/swift-6.4-released/) published September 15, 2026 by Joe Heck and Holly Borla. The release's headline change is that Swift Build is now the default backend in Swift Package Manager, meaning, per the post, that "your projects build the same way on Linux, macOS, and Windows." The GitHub repository for the Swift compiler carries the corresponding `swift-6.4.0-RELEASE` tag, according to...

Author bios for Joe Heck and Holly Borla are also verbatim matches. source-1.html.gz (https://github.com/swiftlang/swift/releases, status 200): confirmed the page contains 'Swift 6.4.0 Release' under tag swift-6.4.0-RELEASE, supporting the article's claim about the release tag. editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabricated or unsourced specifics found. Every proposal number (SE-05xx, SF-0007, ST-002x) and every quoted figure (40x Wasm bridging speedup, NDK 30) traces directly to the swift.org snapshot. The two internal cross-reference links were independently verified to exist and to be topically accurate, not just path-valid: (1) /article/2026-06/12-swift-64-lands-at-wwdc-2026-with-async-defer-anyappleos-availability-and-a-borrowing-iterable-protocol -- confirmed present at that exact path, its title/summary do cover async defer blocks and the borrowing Iterable protocol as WWDC 2026 previews, matching the submission's Background claim. (2) /article/2026-08/25-swift-64-development-snapshots-bring-full-existential-types-and-untyped-throws-to-embedded-swift -- confirmed present at that exact path; its body explicitly defines 'untyped throws' as throwing/catching 'any Error' in Embedded Swift, which lines up with the new GA blog's own Embedded Swift section ('throw and catch any Error'). The submission's claim that these dev-snapshot-only features are 'now part of this stable release' is a reasonable, well-supported synthesis, not a fabrication.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and technical throughout; no editorializing, no sensationalism, no AI self-reference. Reads as straight release-notes journalism appropriate for the News category.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald article covers the Swift 6.4 GA release; searched src/content/articles/2026-09/ for Swift 6.4 coverage and found none. The two claimed cross-references are genuinely distinct prior articles (WWDC 2026 preview from June, Embedded Swift dev-snapshot briefing from August) rather than disguised duplicates -- this article is the first to cover the actual stable release, giving it a distinct angle (GA ships) from both predecessors (preview, dev-snapshot).
concerns: The only automated finding is that swift.org is missing from config/source_allowlist.txt even though its forums.swift.org subdomain has been allowlisted since a 2026-06-12 batch addition for a prior Swift article. This is a config gap, not a content or sourcing problem -- swift.org is Apple's official Swift language project site, the most authoritative possible source for a Swift release announcement. Verified the claims against it directly and found zero discrepancies. Adding swift.org to config/source_allowlist.txt as part of this review's commit to close the gap; overriding the script's suggested APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE since there is no article-content issue for a corrections record to honestly describe.
